newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian market lists first foreign company. [CORRECTED 17:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Palestinian market lists first foreign company. [CORRECTED 17:39 GMT]

text.p: A development firm on Tuesday became the first foreign company listed on the newly-formed Palestinian stock market.

The Palestine Development and Investment Company (PADICO), formed by expatriate Palestinian businessmen in the wake of the 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal, is the 24th company listed on the Palestine Securities Exchange.
Registered in Liberia and based in Amman, the company is capitalised at $200 million, making it the largest listed company.

PADICO owns a 65 percent share in the stock market. It also owns 18 percent of the Palestine Telecommunications Co., which has installed 88,000 phone lines in Palestinian-ruled areas since it began operating five months ago.

The Exchange said in a news release that 15,215 shares worth more than 22,139 Jordanian Dinars ($31,000) were traded on Tuesday. Last week, in its first official report on weekly activities, the exchange said 45,255 shares worth more than 75,000 Jordanian Dinars ($106,000) changed hands.
